title: The Future of MCP — David Soria Parra, Anthropic
talk_summary: Anthropic's MCP lead describes the protocol's evolution and argues agents should combine skills, MCP, and CLIs rather than one connectivity method. The two concrete harness techniques are progressive tool discovery (load tools on demand instead of stuffing all into context) and programmatic tool calling (model writes code against a REPL instead of chaining individual tool calls).

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of loading every tool definition into the context window, expose a tool-search/loader tool and fetch tool schemas only when the model decides it needs them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: use something like tool search to defer the loading of the tools, and start loading the tools when the model needs it
takeaways.numbers: claims 'massive reduction in tool context usage' in Claude Code before/after, no figure given

takeaways.what_they_do: Give the model a REPL/execution environment and let it write a script that composes multiple tool calls, instead of one inference round-trip per tool call.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you want to give the model a repple tool, provide like a like a execution environment ... and just have the model write the code for you

takeaways.what_they_do: Use MCP structured output (or a cheap extraction pass) so tool return types are known, letting the model compose calls and filter JSON programmatically.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's a neat little feature in MCP called structured output that tells you what the return value of the output will be

takeaways.what_they_do: Attach domain knowledge/usage instructions to a tool server so the model learns how to use a large toolset, updatable without plugin/registry changes.

takeaways.technique: Design tools for agents, not REST 1:1 wrappers
takeaways.what_they_do: Avoid auto-converting REST endpoints into tools; design task-shaped tools or expose an execution environment instead.
takeaways.evidence_quote: stop taking rest APIs and put them one-to-one into uh an MCP server ... it just results in horrible things

takeaways.technique: Async task primitive for agent-to-agent work
takeaways.what_they_do: Use long-running task semantics so agents can hand off work asynchronously rather than blocking on synchronous calls.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we need to improve our asynchronous task primitive, which basically is a very fancy way to say we just want to have agent-to-agent communication
